title: i18n: spec still declares `objects.<object>._views.<view>.description` but objectui stopped resolving it (objectui#7219) — declared, accepted, read by nothing
body:
## What changed

objectui#7219 (merged 2026-09-02, maintainer ruling, option B — enforce-or-remove) retired `useObjectLabel().viewDescription()` **and the `_views.<view>.description` catalog convention it resolved**. Its own changeset says an entry left under that key "now resolves nowhere … is simply ignored. Nothing throws."

This repo still declares that key. Measured on `main` at the pin bump for `00d3f09c5`:

- `packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts:203` documents the address `objects.<object>._views.<view_name>.description`.
- `packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts:228` declares `description: z.string().optional().describe('Translated view description')`.

So an ObjectStack author can write the key, the write path accepts it, `check:i18n` is happy, and no renderer reads it. That is the declared-vs-enforced shape the platform files against itself — the one that is worst for AI-authored metadata, which has nothing but the declaration to go on.

## What to decide (not decided here)

1. **Retire the key** on the spec side (ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove, with the ADR-0087 conversion + the generated baselines a spec removal needs), matching objectui's ruling; or
2. **Keep it and restore a reader** — objectui's replacement channel is the `I18nLabel` value authored on the view entry itself, so "keep" would mean routing the catalog key into that same resolution rather than reviving `viewDescription()`; or
3. **Keep it declared as bundle-only data** with an explicit note that no renderer consumes it (weakest option — it is the status quo the ruling just rejected one repo over).

The list-view `description` that DOES reach the screen is a separate, live channel (objectui#7220 relays and resolves it from the view entry), so this is about the catalog address only.

Found while dispositioning the ADR-0087 marker on the `67dadd602a3a → 00d3f09c500c` pin bump (#14511): of the range's 8 declared-breaking entries this is the only one that touches a key `packages/spec` declares. No stored row becomes invalid, so the bump itself prescribes no migration.
